title: Staggered prefill-decode scheduling and tensor-pipeline coordination to maximize NCCL overlap
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: For large models served across tensor and pipeline parallel partitions, end-to-end throughput and P99 latency are limited by suboptimal overlap between compute and inter-GPU communication (NCCL). Prefill (attention KV build) and decode phases have differing compute/comm patterns; naive prefill-then-decode handoffs create idle periods on some ranks and underutilized network slots. We need a scheduler that coordinates tensor/pipeline stages, staggers prefill/decode work, and drives kernel selection to favor attention kernels that expose communication-compute overlap, without regressing accuracy or increasing memory blowout.

Goal: Implement a "staggered prefill-decode" scheduling strategy that: (1) splits prefill into micro-prefill slices aligned to tensor-shard boundaries, (2) schedules decode micro-batches so their NCCL collectives overlap with remaining prefill compute on other pipeline stages, (3) dynamically selects attention kernel variants (streaming-friendly vs fused) based on runtime telemetry to maximize overlap, and (4) gracefully falls back to current static pipeline behavior on topology mismatch or errors.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler integrated into the serving runtime and enabled behind feature-flag 'staggered-scheduling'
End-to-end throughput improvement >= 20% on representative multi-GPU benchmarks (8xA100-like topo) for batch sizes 1-8 compared to baseline
P99 latency reduction >= 15% for decode-heavy workloads with mixed prefill traffic
No accuracy regressions observed on canonical eval prompts (automated eval suite)
Operator-visible metrics: percent NCCL overlap, rank idle time, kernel-selection histogram available in Console
implementation_plan: Design: define micro-prefill unit (mini-token groups) and mapping to tensor sharding offsets
Runtime: add a scheduling layer that tracks per-rank state (prefill remaining, decode queued) and issues prefill micro-slices or decode steps based on heuristics and backpressure
NCCL overlap: issue non-blocking collectives where possible; use separate CUDA streams for comm vs compute; ensure NCCL operations are posted early
Kernel selection hook: expose runtime hint that chooses attention kernel variant based on predicted overlap potential (latency-critical vs throughput-critical)
Fallbacks: topology checker and deterministic fallback path that disables staggering for unsupported configs
Testing: unit tests for ordering, integration tests across 2/4/8 GPU topologies, stress test with synthetic mixed prefill/decode load
Observability: new telemetry tags (staggered_enabled, micro_prefill_size), dashboards and perf tests linked
Rollout: canary on Dedicated pools with feature-flag; monitor metrics for 48h before ramping
experiments_and_results: Local 4-GPU perf run (A100-40GB emulation) with micro-prefill=16 tokens: throughput +18%, P99 decode -12% (github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/compare/exp-staggered-aug)
8-GPU cluster run (internal lab) with micro-prefill=8: throughput +28%, avg NCCL overlap increased from 34% to 67% (dashboard: dashboards.redwood.internal/s/multi-gpu-staggered)
Kernel selection ablation: fused attention variant improves latency but reduces NCCL overlap on longer sequences; hybrid policy (streaming kernel when overlap <50%) yields best tradeoff
Memory tradeoff: micro-prefill introduces transient peak mem +4-6% on tensor-sharded ranks — within Dedicated pool headroom for targeted SKUs
risks_and_mitigations: Increased scheduler complexity -> harder to debug deadlocks: mitigation: deterministic replay mode + integration tests and watchdog timeouts
Memory pressure on hot ranks due to micro-prefill slices -> mitigation: adaptive micro-prefill sizing and reject-small-microprefill when memory_margin < 10%
Topology mismatches (heterogeneous GPUs / NVLink gaps) can reduce benefits -> mitigation: topology-aware cost model and auto-disable flag per-pool
NCCL version sensitivity: older NCCL releases may not expose required non-blocking semantics -> mitigation: require NCCL >= 2.12 for feature flag, add runtime check

2025-08-22 - Liam Chen: Spike complete. Implemented prototype micro-prefill and observed strong NCCL overlap in synthetic runs. Created PR #2789. Current tradeoff is +5% mem transient on tensor ranks.
2025-08-29 - Design review (Maya Patel): Approved approach with caveat to add deterministic replay for debugging. Suggested adding an operator-visible metric for 'staggered_mode' per-request.

2025-09-01 - Performance review (Jules Moreno): Integration run across 8 GPUs showed 28% throughput gain. Noted variance increase at high concurrency; suggested adaptive micro-prefill tuning and upper bound on queued decode steps.

2025-09-02 - Liam Chen: Enabled canary on 'dedicated-us-west' pool behind feature-flag. Monitoring NCCL overlap, rank_idle_pct, and memory_margin. Early telemetry looks stable. Next: prepare rollback runbook and automation for auto-disable if memory_margin < 8%
